description: emflow is Rebase Energy's Python software for constructing and evaluating sequential decision problems in energy systems. It separates datasets, environments, objectives, predictors, simulators, optimisers and agents, using Gymnasium-style interactions and time-aware data access. Inputs include energy-asset definitions, historical or forecast series, feature specifications and policy settings; outputs are experiment results and metrics such as forecast error or trading revenue. Geographic coverage and time resolution follow each configured problem. Public source is free under MIT. A limitation is that valid evaluation depends on data availability at each decision time and on defensible objectives; a reproducible run does not prove a policy will transfer to future conditions. External benchmark data and solver dependencies must be checked separately. emflow can support forecast-driven dispatch and energy-market simulations, complementary to PyPSA (model-pypsa). The README documents its component model, experiment sweeps and historical forecasting or trading benchmarks. No market data or experiment was downloaded or run.
